summary.text: An enzyme is a biological macromolecule, usually a protein, that speeds up chemical reactions without being consumed.
Enzymes work by lowering a reaction's activation energy, often by factors of millions.
Nearly all metabolic processes in a cell depend on enzyme catalysis to run at biologically relevant rates.

facts.label: First discovery
facts.value: Anselme Payen found the enzyme diastase in 1833

facts.label: Naming habit
facts.value: Names usually end in -ase, as in lactase

facts.label: Substrates
facts.value: The molecules enzymes act on, converted into products

facts.label: RNA catalysts
facts.value: Ribozymes are sometimes classified as enzymes despite being RNA

items.prompt: A cook sprinkles papain onto a tough cut of meat. What does it do?

options.label: It adds fat so that the meat feels softer once cooked
It heats the meat from within, so it cooks more quickly
It breaks down proteins in the meat, improving the texture
It coats the meat so that water cannot escape the surface

items.explain: Papain is a proteolytic enzyme used in meat tenderizers to hydrolyze proteins and improve texture.

items.prompt: One enzyme molecule helps convert a substrate, then goes on to convert another, and another. Why can it keep working?

options.label: It speeds the reaction up without being consumed by it
It is slowly consumed, but the cell makes more each cycle
It changes the final balance of the reaction toward product
It joins permanently to the product and travels on with it

items.explain: Enzymes accelerate reactions without being consumed, and they are regenerated at the end of each cycle.

items.prompt: Without help, a reaction would take millions of years, but with an enzyme it finishes in milliseconds. How does the enzyme manage this?

options.label: It pushes the final balance of the reaction toward more product
It supplies extra reactant so that the reaction has more to use
It heats the cell so that molecules collide far more often
It lowers the activation energy that the reaction must overcome

items.explain: Enzymes raise the reaction rate by lowering its activation energy, and they do not change the overall equilibrium.

items.prompt: A lab heats an enzyme solution far beyond its best temperature, and the reaction it drives stops. What is the likeliest reason?

options.label: The substrate runs out because heat uses it up faster
The enzyme loses its structure, which ends its function
The enzyme speeds up so much that it burns itself out
The warmer solution makes every reaction in it stop at once

items.explain: Outside optimal conditions enzymes can lose their structure through denaturation, which means a loss of function.

items.prompt: A mixture holds yeast extract but no living yeast cells, and it still ferments sugar. What does this show?

options.label: Fermentation can happen without living cells, through enzymes
Fermentation needs a vital force found only in living yeast
The extract must hide a few living yeast cells doing the work
Sugar ferments by itself when left to stand, with no help at all

items.explain: Buchner found that sugar was fermented by yeast extract with no living cells present, which showed cell-free fermentation by an enzyme he named zymase.

items.prompt: A drug lowers the activity of a harmful enzyme without removing it. What kind of molecule is the drug acting as?

options.label: An activator, which enhances the enzyme's activity
A substrate, which the enzyme turns into a product
An isozyme, a different enzyme doing the same reaction
An inhibitor, which diminishes the enzyme's activity

items.explain: Enzyme activity can be enhanced by activators or diminished by inhibitors, and many inhibitors serve as drugs or poisons.
